scenery = the painted backgrounds and structures on a stage
props = objects that actors use on stage or on set
backstage = the area behind the stage, not seen by the audience
tragedy = a serious play with a sad ending, often about a hero's downfall
farce = a comic play based on ridiculous situations and mistakes
West End = London's main commercial theatre district
fringe theatre = small, experimental theatre outside the commercial mainstream
amateur dramatics = theatre performed by non-professionals, often locally
orchestra pit = the lowered area in front of the stage where musicians play
piracy = illegal copying or sharing of films, music or books
symphony = a long piece of music for a full orchestra, usually in several movements
concerto = a piece for a solo instrument with orchestral accompaniment
chamber music = classical music for a small group of players, often one to a part
aria = a song for one voice in an opera, with orchestral accompaniment
virtuoso = a musician of outstanding technical skill
cover version = a new recording of a song first performed by someone else
busker = a musician who performs in the street for money
acoustic = played without electronic amplification
headliner = the main act that a concert or festival is built around
support act = a band or singer who performs before the main artist
